brief.t: As of 2026-11-20, old-crop (2026/27) unfixed call **sales** are 63.5k contracts (-4,789 w/w, -10,341 over 8 weeks) and old-crop unfixed **purchases** 20.5k (-6,543 w/w). Against the same week of the last five seasons, sales are at the 73rd percentile (avg 68.2k) and purchases at the 27th (avg 30.2k). Beyond this season, merchants hold 11.2k of new-crop sales and 40.2k of new-crop purchases.

Net old-crop on-call is +42,924 (mill side). In old-crop COT, producers/merchants/processors/users hold 73.2k long and 184.5k short (net -111,311, -2,102 w/w). Their long/short ratio of 0.40 sits at the 15th percentile of the last three years: **commercials hold relatively little long cover, so fixing the mill-side book is more likely to need buying in the market**. The net and the ratio matter more than gross longs, which include calendar-spread legs held by trade houses. On the other side, total unfixed purchases of 60.7k (-1,671 over 8 weeks) compare with 210.6k PMU shorts and 20.4k swap-dealer shorts — producer fixing is latent selling, whether it runs through PMU hedges or swap structures.

Front contract **December 2026** is 0.6 weeks from first notice, with 345 unfixed sales and 1.0k unfixed purchases against 538 open interest. Next: March 2027 with 32.4k unfixed sales. The Dec/Mar spread is -3.17¢, +0.39¢ on the week.

Old-crop unfixed sales of 6.61m bales equal 15% of USDA's 2026/27 world trade forecast (44.8m, November 2026). USDA sees Brazil exporting 16.0m bales vs the US 12.3m. US export sales (week of 2026-11-19): 4.63m running bales unshipped, China 6%.
Managed money is net long 49.0k (-6,384 w/w; 3-yr COT index 69). Spec positioning is not at an extreme.
